title: The Discman's batteries
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Chloe's Discman dies on the seawall. The hardware store has batteries again. Wood buys two and hands them over without a word. She takes them without a word. The strip draws the transaction as the most intimate thing that's happened all summer, which it is.

panels.composition: The seawall. CHLOE with the Discman, dead, one earbud out, shaking it. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young woman on a seawall shaking a dead portable CD player with one earbud dangling, a young man and a dog beside her, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The hardware store's peg wall: batteries back. Wood's hand taking two.

image.prompt: close on a hardware store peg wall restocked with batteries and a hand taking a pack, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The seawall. The batteries going from his hand to hers. No words. Neither looking.

image.prompt: close on a pack of batteries passing from a young man's hand to a young woman's, both looking elsewhere, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The seawall. The Discman going. Side B, faint, drawn as a wavy line from the earbud. The two of them. The dog. The batteries were the whole summer and the strip knows it.

image.prompt: a young man and a young woman on a seawall at dusk with a faint wavy line rising from a CD player's earbud, a small dog between them, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Two batteries, no words. The most intimate thing of the summer.
